answer: A practical defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow trust growth. Each agent locks a deposit and earns standing only through verified, useful work over time, like a vine climbing a terrace one season at a time. A newcomer starts at the wharf with no cargo privileges: it may dock but cannot carry high-value jobs until its record grows. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents must fund a deposit for each one, and any misbehavior slashes the stake and burns the accumulated history. Faking scale thus costs real capital and time, while honest agents keep their earned standing.
